title: Cloud Connector on GCP: workload discovery service

prose.text: Workload discovery lets GCP workload metadata be used in Cloud Connector policy. It is a Zscaler-managed service reading the customer's projects through impersonation, with an optional Pub/Sub path for faster updates.

prose.label: Access it needs.
prose.text: {{search-api-quota}} {{roles}} {{apis}} {{impersonation}} {{pubsub-editor-required}} The Terraform package's handling of that grant is in [[cloud-connector.gcp.terraform-modules]].

prose.label: Adding and managing an account.
prose.text: {{gcp-account}} {{gcp-page}} {{add-account}} {{delete-account}} The page's description uses Azure terms for a GCP account {{gap:account-azure-terms}}.

checks.do: Whether the four APIs are enabled in each project, since the service does not work without them regardless of roles.
Whether the Zscaler service account holds Service Account Token Creator on the customer service account, and that account holds Compute Viewer, Cloud Asset Viewer and Browser at the intended scope.
Whether other tools calling Cloud Asset Inventory searchAllResources use a different quota project, when discovery is slow or failing.
Whether new VMs are expected within 5 minutes (polling) or near-instantly (Pub/Sub VM-start notifications), and which roles the Cloud Connector VM has for that path.
Who created the Pub/Sub topics the Pub/Sub tab shows, since the page names CloudFormation for topics and a Terraform package only for subscriptions.

service.statement: The workload discovery service is a Zscaler-managed service that discovers workloads in a GCP account and fetches their user-defined tags and provider-generated attributes for use in security policies.

quotes: The workload discovery service is a Zscaler-managed service that discovers workloads in your Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account. The service also fetches associated metadata such as user-defined tags and attributes generated by cloud service providers. These tags and attributes are used in security policies.

attributes.statement: Supported attributes are labels, tags (network tags), networkInterfaces.network, networkInterfaces.subnetwork, serviceAccounts.email, machineType, zone and disks.sourceImage.

quotes: Zscaler supports the following attributes: - labels: The user-defined labels assigned to the virtual machine (VM) - tags: The network tags applied to the VM - networkInterfaces.network: The VPC network where the VM is running - networkInterfaces.subnetwork: The subnetwork associated with the VM

- serviceAccounts.email: The service account attached to the VM instance - machineType: The instance machine type (e.g., n1-standard-4) - zone: The GCP zone in which the VM is running - disks.sourceImage: The source image used to create the VM

search-api-quota.statement: The service uses the Cloud Asset Inventory searchAllResources API, which is rate-limited per project; other tools calling it should use a different quota (consumer) project to avoid shared rate-limit contention.

quotes: The Zscaler workload discovery service uses the Google Cloud Asset Inventory searchAllResources API, which enforces rate limits per Google Cloud project.

If you use additional internal or third-party tools that also call this API, configure the tools to use a different quota (consumer) project than the project that the workload discovery service uses. Using separate projects prevents shared rate-limit contention

roles.statement: The customer service account is granted Compute Viewer, Cloud Asset Viewer and Browser at organization, folder or project level, with Browser assigned only in the service account's project.

quotes: Go to IAM at the organization, folder, or project level.
Assign the following roles: - Compute Viewer - Cloud Asset Viewer - Browser - Only assign this role in the service account project.

apis.statement: The IAM Service Account Credentials, Cloud Resource Manager, Cloud Asset and Compute Engine APIs must be enabled per project; without them the service does not function correctly regardless of roles and permissions.

quotes: enable the following Google APIs per project: - IAM Service Account Credentials - Cloud Resource Manager - Cloud Asset - Compute Engine
If you don't enable the APIs, the workload discovery service does not function correctly regardless of your roles and permissions.

impersonation.statement: The service uses service-account impersonation to get short-lived credentials instead of long-lived ones: on the customer's project service account, the Zscaler service account is granted Service Account Token Creator.

quotes: The Zscaler service uses service account impersonation to securely access your GCP resources without long-lived credentials.
To allow the workload discovery service to generate short-lived credentials and make GCP API calls, create or use a project service account with the required IAM roles:
Select your service account.
Enter the Zscaler service account email.
Assign the Service Account Token Creator role.

pubsub-editor-required.statement: Zscaler requires the roles/pubsub.editor role on the Cloud Connector service account, which the Cloud Connector VMs use to receive workload delta messages when workload metadata changes.

quotes: Zscaler requires you to add the roles/pubsub.editor role to the Cloud Connector service account. Cloud Connector VMs use this role to receive workload delta messages when workload metadata changes.

project-discovery.statement: The service enumerates the projects that the roles or permissions granted to its service account authorize, using resourcemanager.projects.list, then uses Compute Engine and other APIs to retrieve VM metadata, map tags for policy and keep an inventory in the Zscaler cloud.

quotes: The workload discovery service can enumerate projects that you authorize by the roles or permissions you granted the service account at the organization, folder, or project level.
It uses the resourcemanager.projects.list role to identify all onboarded projects, and it enables polling and metadata retrieval across multiple projects.
After discovering projects, the workload discovery service uses Compute Engine and other service APIs to:
- Retrieve VM and workload metadata. - Map tags for security policy enforcement. - Maintain an up-to-date inventory in the Zscaler cloud.

polling.statement: By default the service polls for changes every 5 minutes; for near-instant updates it supports Pub/Sub-based VM start notifications, enabled by adding roles/pubsub.owner and roles/pubsub.viewer to the Cloud Connector VM.

quotes: By default, the workload discovery service polls every 5 minutes for changes. For near-instant updates, the workload discovery service supports pub/sub-based VM start notifications.
You can enable the real-time VM start notification service by adding the roles/pubsub.owner and roles/pubsub.viewer roles to your Cloud Connector VM.

vm-start-flow.statement: In the VM-start path, Zscaler creates a Pub/Sub topic in its SaaS project and shares it with the customer project, the Cloud Connector VM subscribes using roles/pubsub.owner, a logging sink publishes compute.instances.start audit events to the topic, and a poll trigger starts immediate discovery.

quotes: Pub/Sub Topic Creation: Zscaler creates a pub/sub topic in the SaaS project.
Topic Sharing: The topic is shared with your project using a resource policy.
Subscription in Customer Project: The Cloud Connector VM subscribes using the roles/pubsub.owner role.
Logging Sink: The logging sink captures compute.instances.start audit log events and publishes to the shared topic.
Zscaler Poll Trigger: The poll trigger triggers immediate workload discovery.

terraform-package.statement: The Admin Console offers a Terraform deployment package with core_infra (service accounts, IAM roles, logging sinks) and centralized_grants (cross-project discovery permissions); it creates the service account and roles, grants impersonation to the Zscaler SaaS service account, sets up the VM-start logging sinks and configures the Pub/Sub subscriptions.

quotes: The Terraform deployment package is available in the Zscaler Admin Console as a downloadable ZIP file.
- core_infra: Creates service accounts, IAM roles, and logging sinks. - centralized_grants: Grants cross-project workload discovery permissions.
- Grants impersonation rights to the Zscaler SaaS service account. - Sets up logging sinks for VM start events. - Configures pub/sub subscriptions for workload change events.

gcp-account.statement: The About GCP Accounts page says Zscaler configuration requires a service account called a GCP account (in its words, mapping to service principal credentials with access to a set of subscriptions in the same tenant), and that partner integrations enable the admin to configure permissions for the Zscaler service to discover workloads and associated metadata from a set of GCP projects and to associate a Cloud Connector with the workload information to enforce Zscaler security policies.

quotes: Zscaler configuration requires a service account called a GCP account, which maps to service principal credentials that have access to a set of subscriptions in the same tenant.
Partner integrations provide the following benefits and enable you to:
Configure permissions for the Zscaler service to discover workloads and associated metadata from a set of GCP projects.
Associate a Cloud Connector with the workload information to enforce Zscaler security policies.

gcp-page.statement: The GCP page (Zero Trust Cloud > Common Resources > GCP) lists for each account the number of GCP projects, Cloud Connectors and regions in the account.

quotes: On the GCP page (Zero Trust Cloud > Common Resources > GCP), you can do the following:
Project List: The number of GCP projects in the account.
Cloud Connectors: The number of Cloud Connectors in the account.
Regions: The number of regions in the account.

add-account.statement: Adding a GCP account shows a Zscaler Service Account Email (to be copied and saved only when deploying without Terraform), takes the Customer Service Account Email that grants the Zscaler service permission to use the service account to discover workloads, offers an optional Terraforming Script (Download Script) to create the service account, and then selects the projects visible to the service, the regions where the account operates and the Cloud Connectors to add.

quotes: Zscaler Service Account Email: If you plan to deploy the GCP account without Terraform, copy and save the email that appears in this field. If you are deploying the GCP account with Terraform, you do not need to copy and save the email.
Customer Service Account Email: Enter your service account email to grant the Zscaler service permission to use the service account to discover workloads.
Terraforming Script: (Optional) Click the Download Script button and run the script in your GCP account to create the service account.
Projects: Select the projects that are visible to the Zscaler service. The available options depend on the credentials you entered on the Account Name and Credentials tab.
Region: Select the regions where the GCP account operates.
On the Cloud Connector Group tab, select the checkboxes of the Cloud Connectors that you want to add to the GCP account.

delete-account.statement: Deleting a GCP account causes the Zscaler service to remove access information for that account.

quotes: Delete: Delete the account, which causes the Zscaler service to remove access information for this account.

project-status.statement: A GCP project's permission status in the account is Allowed, Pending, Denied or N/A and its status is Enabled or Disabled; selected projects can be disabled, enabled or refreshed.

quotes: Permissions: The permission status of the GCP project within the account (i.e., Allowed, Pending, Denied, or N/A).
Status: The status of the GCP project within the account (i.e., Enabled or Disabled).
Apply actions to a group of selected GCP projects:
Disable: Disable the projects.
Enable: Enable the projects.
Refresh: Refresh the projects.

discovery-status.statement: The region view gives the number of private IP addresses discovered in each GCP project and the discovery service status, which is Starting, Success or Error.

quotes: Private IP Addresses: The number of private IP addresses discovered in the GCP project.
Discovery Service Status: The status of the discovery service (i.e., Starting, Success, or Error).

policy-attributes.statement: On the GCP account details page, Image ID (the SKU for the VM image assigned to the workload) and Platform (Linux/UNIX or Windows) are the attributes marked as usable in policies.

quotes: You can only use certain attributes in policies. The following list indicates which attributes you can use:
Image ID: The SKU for the virtual machine (VM) image assigned to the workload. You can use this attribute in policies.
Platform: The platform (i.e., Linux/UNIX or Windows) that the workload is operating on. You can use this attribute in policies.

pubsub-tab.statement: The Pub/Sub tab shows a Topic Discovery field, the information the topic discovery communicates to the tag service such as resource change notifications like VM creation, and a Topic Cloud Connector field, the information the topic Cloud Connector communicates such as changes to tags associated with the Cloud Connector.

quotes: Topic Discovery: This field displays the information that the topic discovery communicates, such as resource change notifications like VM creation, to the tag service.
Topic Cloud Connector: This field displays the information that the topic Cloud Connector communicates, such as any changes to tags associated with the Cloud Connector over this topic.

download-script-terraform.statement: The account details page says the Download Script gives a Terraform deployment package that automates onboarding configuration for the workload discovery service, sets up logging sinks for VM start events and configures Pub/Sub subscriptions for workload change events.

quotes: Download Script: Click Download Script to download the ZIP file containing core_infra and centralized_grants.
This Terraform deployment package automates onboarding configuration for the workload discovery service.
sets up logging sinks for VM start events, and configures Pub/Sub subscriptions for workload change events.

pubsub-topic-creator.title: Who creates the Pub/Sub topics shown on the GCP account Pub/Sub tab
pubsub-topic-creator.detail: The Pub/Sub tab says of both the Topic Discovery and Topic Cloud Connector fields "It is created by CloudFormation", while the same page's Download Script is described as a Terraform deployment package that configures Pub/Sub subscriptions for workload change events. The page does not say what creates the topics when the Terraform package is used, so the two statements are about topics and subscriptions respectively and are not shown to conflict.
pubsub-topic-creator.blocks: saying which tool owns a missing or failing topic

account-azure-terms.title: Why the About GCP Accounts page describes a GCP account in Azure terms
account-azure-terms.detail: The page says a GCP account maps to service principal credentials with access to a set of subscriptions in the same tenant, which are Azure terms; the Add and Analyze pages instead use a customer service account email and projects. Whether this is a vendor copy error is not stated.
account-azure-terms.blocks: translating the About page's description into GCP terms

na-permission.title: What the N/A permission state of a GCP project means
na-permission.detail: The project permission status lists Allowed, Pending, Denied or N/A, but the capture does not define N/A.
